newsitem.title: JAPAN: Suzutan raided in suspected insider trading case.
newsitem.headline: Suzutan raided in suspected insider trading case.

text.p: Suzutan Co Ltd said on Friday that prosecutors raided its headquarters in Nagoya on Tuesday in connection with suspected illegal insider trading by former officials, including former president Katsurao Suzui.
Tokai Bank Ltd, through which Suzutan conducts a major portion of its financial transactions, said on Friday that its headquarters were also raided by prosecutors on Tueday.
A bank spokesman said, however, that the search was not conducted on suspicion that the bank or bank officials were involved in insider trading.

Earlier this week, government sources told Reuters that the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission filed accusations against former Suzutan officials for allegedly selling Suzutan shares before disclosing possible losses at a subsidiary and the possibility that the company held unpayable, guaranteed debts.

Suzui, one of the officials accused, resigned from his post as president of the women's apparel retailer in March. He earlier acknowledged that he sold 1.01 million Suzutan shares prior to an announcement of a loss for the 1994/95 business year, but said he did not regard this as improper.
